basis: Ichthyosis and congenital digital abnormalities define the syndrome; mouth and lip shape changes do not establish gastrointestinal dysfunction.
Inherited glomerular disease with nephrotic proteinuria, podocyte injury and progressive kidney failure.
Skeletal anomalies, cutis laxa and developmental impairment define syndrome; ptosis/strabismus 30-79%; dental enamel defects and hepatic adenoma omitted by cap.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Disease of the vestibulocochlear nerve or central auditory pathways, defined by auditory system involvement.
Benign neoplasm originating in the ear; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, speech delay, ataxia and spasticity; no established systemic metabolic disorder.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma; blood and marrow lineage establishes haematologic involvement, and lymphoma requires the immune axis.
Dengue infection with defining thrombocytopenia, hemorrhagic tendency and capillary plasma leakage; shock is a minority subtype.
Proximal gastric polyposis is defining and present in 32/32 annotated patients; associated gastric carcinoma remains within the same axis.
Atypical proliferation confined to breast lobules; breast has no axis.
Malignant bone-forming mesenchymal tumor, usually arising in bone; pulmonary metastasis is not a defining or uniformly common feature.
GRXCR1-related nonsyndromic hearing loss; hearing impairment in 10/10 annotated patients.
Foveal developmental abnormality with reduced visual acuity, nystagmus and refractive abnormalities.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow defined by a recurrent chromosomal translocation.
Mild factor IX deficiency causes a coagulation disorder; chronic joint damage is not typical of this mild form.
Inherited hair disorder characterized by sparse, brittle, slow-growing hair and patchy alopecia.
Visceral myopathy with intestinal dysmotility and external ophthalmoplegia; skeletal myopathy and atrophy occur in 80-99%; neuropathy frequency unspecified.
Phenylalanine metabolism disorder umbrella; neurologic injury varies with subtype, biochemical severity and treatment, so common established injury is not assured.
Familial mitral valve prolapse with possible regurgitation; skeletal and skin findings lack evidence of common substantial damage.
Sulfur mustard directly injures skin, ocular surfaces and respiratory epithelium; marrow suppression occurs chiefly with severe systemic exposure.
IgM-producing lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma involving marrow; direct lung lesions and other organ injuries are occasional; respiratory insufficiency alone is insufficient.
Relative polycythemia from dehydration combines hemoconcentration with disturbed body-water homeostasis; no additional organ injury is inherent.
Acute infection-triggered brain dysfunction; a postinfectious trigger alone does not establish direct CNS infection or a uniformly immune-mediated mechanism.
Inherited tubulointerstitial kidney disease with defining hyperuricemia; gout is a separately diagnosed manifestation and does not justify musculoskeletal involvement.
